prs.body:
## High Level Overview of Change

Remove the per-insertion heap allocations from `Batch::preflight`. The duplicate-inner-transaction and duplicate-sequence/ticket checks used an `std::unordered_set` and an `std::unordered_map` of `std::unordered_set`s; they are now `std::flat_set`s backed by a `boost::container::small_vector` sized to `kMaxBatchTxCount`, so neither container ever leaves inline storage.

## Context of Change

`Batch::preflight` runs for every submitted and relayed Batch, including those about to be rejected, and the two containers it used allocate per node (and, for the map, per distinct account) to hold at most eight entries. The map of sets is flattened to a set of `(account, sequence-or-ticket)` pairs: pair membership was the only query, and the preceding `temSEQ_AND_TICKET` checks already guarantee exactly one of `Sequence` and `TicketSequence` is set, so the two insert sites collapse into one. Sequences and tickets keep sharing one key space per account, and the checks run at the same point in the per-inner loop, so every result code is unchanged. No amendment is needed.

## API Impact

- [ ] Public API: New feature (new methods and/or new fields)
- [ ] Public API: Breaking change (in general, breaking changes should only impact the next api_version)
- [x] `libxrpl` change (any change that may affect `libxrpl` or dependents of `libxrpl`)
- [ ] Peer protocol change (must be backward compatible or bump the peer protocol version)

The change is internal to `Batch::preflight`; no `libxrpl` interface changes.

## Before / After

1. Improvement to existing functionality.
2. Memory allocation behavior of `Batch::preflight`; transaction results are unchanged.
3. Preflight of Batch transactions on the submit and relay paths (`checkValidity`, `TxQ::apply`, ledger building).
4. No effect on concurrent processing: no locks, threads, or async work are involved.

## Test Plan

Existing `xrpl.app.Batch` unit tests, which assert the `temREDUNDANT` and `temSEQ_AND_TICKET` results for duplicate inners, sequences, and tickets across all four batch modes.

> The alternative was a field in the outer's metadata, but the outer's leaf is inserted before its inner transactions run and OpenView::rawTxInsert does not replace a leaf.

Interesting 

Yeah, conceptually if the outer transaction's only effect is to add/queue the inners, then backtracking and updating the metadata is a little murky and sets a precedent. 

On the other hand, you have a result attached to the the known outer txn id, which is more easy to consume than having to retrieve and parse the whole ledger's transactions which is the naive consequence barring updating rpc handlers to do the scan, potentially using indexes. 

Using metadata would probably also save some bytes, reusing existing txn/serialization instead of a new key/leaf. 

Murky 🤔 

Then again, maybe transactions are just the atoms, and batches, as long as they are comprised of contiguous atoms, can be thought of some bigger unit: transactions / batches / ledgers.

prs.body:
## High Level Overview of Change

Adds the `BatchV2` amendment and a `ttBATCH_RESULT` (`BatchResult`) pseudo-transaction. When a `Batch` applies with `tesSUCCESS` in a closed ledger, `applyTransaction` inserts a `BatchResult` right after the batch's inner transactions. It carries the outer's ID in `sfParentBatchID` and lists every inner transaction the batch attempted, in order, as `sfTransactionHash` and `sfEngineResultCode`.

## Context of Change

An inner transaction that fails with a `tem`, `tef` or `ter` code leaves nothing in the ledger, and neither does any inner transaction of a rolled-back `tfAllOrNothing` batch. The outer's metadata covers only its own fee and sequence, so the only record of what a batch did is the `BatchTrace` log line on the node that applied it. #8164 keeps those results in a node-local table; this puts them in the ledger, so every node, Clio and explorer reads the same answer.

The record cannot be agreed in the transaction set like `ttFEE` or `ttAMENDMENT`, because its content exists only after execution. It is generated during the ledger build, as the inner transactions already are, from the outer ID and the inner IDs and results only, so every node produces the same leaf. It is inserted into the view the outer applied to, after the batch view is committed or dropped, so a rollback cannot remove it. The alternative was a field in the outer's metadata, but the outer's leaf is inserted before its inner transactions run and `OpenView::rawTxInsert` does not replace a leaf.

An entry was applied when its result is `tes` or `tec` and the batch was not rolled back; an inner transaction missing from `sfBatchResults` was never attempted. `sfEngineResultCode` is `INT32` because `tem`, `tef` and `ter` codes are negative.

`isPseudoTx` covers the new type, so it cannot be submitted or relayed, and `Change` preflight rejects it with `temINVALID` on any view, including from a proposed transaction set. Ledger replay skips it, and replaying the outer regenerates it.

## API Impact

- [x] Public API: New feature (new methods and/or new fields)
- [x] `libxrpl` change (any change that may affect `libxrpl` or dependents of `libxrpl`)

`tx`, `ledger` and the transaction streams return the new `BatchResult` transaction type once `BatchV2` is enabled.

## Future Tasks

- Amend XLS-0056 to specify `BatchResult`.

prs.body:
## High Level Overview of Change

Mask `secret`, `seed`, `seed_hex`, and `passphrase` fields when HTTP batch RPC requests are rejected before handler execution. Masking traverses nested objects and arrays so sensitive values are not echoed in error responses or debug reply logs.

Closes #7461.

## Context of Change

The normal RPC handler-error path masks sensitive fields before attaching request data to an error response. Eight early-error paths in HTTP batch processing instead copied the request item directly into the response, bypassing that masking.

This change applies masking only to the copied request data used by those error paths. It leaves the original request available to subsequent processing and does not sanitize successful handler output, which can legitimately contain generated wallet credentials.

## API Impact

This is a non-breaking public API bug fix. The affected error responses preserve their existing structure, codes, messages, IDs, and non-sensitive request fields; only sensitive field values are replaced with `<masked>`. `API-CHANGELOG.md` documents the change.

## Before / After

Before, an early failure such as an invalid `api_version`, forbidden method, overload, malformed method, malformed `ripplerpc`, or non-object batch item could echo sensitive request values verbatim.

After, sensitive fields in the echoed request copy are masked recursively. Other batch items continue to execute normally unless the client is already over the resource limit.

## Test Plan

- Verified the regression tests fail against the original handler with the sensitive sentinels present.
- Built the standard `xrpld` target in the repository's Nix CI environment with GCC 15.2.
- Ran all automatic RPC and server suites: 51 suites, 341 cases, 78,050 assertions, zero failures.
- Ran explicit `clang-tidy` on the changed C++ files.
- Ran applicable pre-commit checks, including the pinned formatter, include-style checks, spelling, and Markdown formatting.

- One batch can create a smart escrow and finish it.
- An inner finish runs its contract, and the batch mode acts on the answer: approve, reject under independent, reject under all-or-nothing.
- The outer fee covers the inners' Gas and Bytecode charges: one drop short is refused, the exact fee is accepted. A flat per-inner fee in `Batch::calculateBaseFee` fails this test (checked by temporarily making that change).

These are Beast tests rather than gtest because gtest's `TxTest` does not apply a Batch's inners.

## API Impact

None (tests only).

prs.body:
## High Level Overview of Change

A Payment inside the `RawTransactions` of a Batch now follows the `DeliverMax` rule on output and input, like a top-level Payment. `simulate` and `submit` with `tx_blob` follow it too.

- `insertDeliverMax` applies the rule to each inner Payment of a Batch, so every method that already calls it renders inner Payments with `DeliverMax`. `simulate` and `submit` with `tx_blob` now call it on the `tx_json` they return.
- `removeDeliverMax` replaces the alias handling in `checkPayment`, maps `DeliverMax` to `Amount` in inner Payments as well, and runs before `checkFee` (and before `autofillTx` in `simulate`).

Fixes #8557

## Context of Change

`insertDeliverMax` only acted on a top-level `ttPAYMENT`, and `checkPayment` only aliased a top-level Payment. `DeliverMax` is not an `SField`, so `STParsedJSON` rejected it in an inner Payment as an unknown field. While tracing the callers I found that `simulate` had no `DeliverMax` handling at all, and `doSubmit` rendered `tx_json` without calling `insertDeliverMax`.

The alias is resolved before `checkFee` because `getTxFee` parses `tx_json` to compute the fee. A Batch fee depends on its inner transactions, so an unresolved inner `DeliverMax` fails that parse and the autofilled fee falls back to the reference fee. `autofillTx` in `simulate` has the same dependency for a multi-signed Payment.

## API Impact

- [ ] Public API: New feature (new methods and/or new fields)
- [x] Public API: Breaking change (in general, breaking changes should only impact the next api_version)
- [ ] `libxrpl` change (any change that may affect `libxrpl` or dependents of `libxrpl`)
- [ ] Peer protocol change (must be backward compatible or bump the peer protocol version)

In API version 2, inner Payments and the `tx_json` returned by `simulate` and by `submit` with `tx_blob` now carry only `DeliverMax`, not `Amount`, matching every other Payment in v2. API version 1 gains `DeliverMax` next to `Amount`. `DeliverMax` is now accepted where it was rejected. Entries are in `API-CHANGELOG.md`.

reviews.author: xrplf-ai-reviewer[bot]
reviews.body: This change extends DeliverMax handling to inner Batch Payments and to simulate/submit responses, consolidating the alias logic into insertDeliverMax/removeDeliverMax. The refactor is coherent: removeDeliverMax is correctly short-circuited on a differing Amount/DeliverMax error, is applied before fee autofill (matching the stated rationale), and insertDeliverMax's Batch branch mutates inner RawTransaction objects by reference as needed. Call sites in TransactionSign.cpp, Simulate.cpp, and Submit.cpp appear consistently wired to match the CHANGELOG claims, and the accompanying tests exercise sign/submit/simulate/tx/transaction_entry/ledger/account_tx across API versions. I did not find a confident correctness or security bug introduced by the added lines.

reviews.author: xrplf-ai-reviewer[bot]
reviews.body: The change plumbs DeliverMax handling into inner Batch Payments and into simulate/submit output rendering, and adds solid coverage for those specific paths (Batch via sign+submit, simulate, submit with tx_blob). The one thing I can't verify from the diff alone is call order in TransactionSign.cpp: checkPayment() had its DeliverMax-alias logic deleted and now only checks `txJson.isMember(jss::Amount)`, while the new `removeDeliverMax()` call is inserted elsewhere in transactionPreProcessImpl/transactionSubmitMultiSigned. If checkPayment still runs before that insertion point, a bare top-level Payment signed via `sign`/`submit_multisigned` with only `DeliverMax` (no `Amount`) would now be rejected with a missing-field error — a regression on exactly the feature this PR adds. None of the new tests catch this because they all route around checkPayment's Amount check (Batch's top-level type isn't Payment so checkPayment short-circuits; simulate and tx_blob submit never call checkPayment at all).

reviewCommentsList.body: This only visits the canonical `RawTransaction` wrapper, but batches accepted before `fixBatchV1_2` can use other object wrappers (see `src/test/app/Batch_test.cpp:5951-6012`), and such transactions may also exist in historical ledgers. Their inner Payments will therefore still be rendered with `Amount`, and `DeliverMax` input remains unrecognized when those rules are active, contradicting the “each inner Payment” behavior. Traverse every object-valued wrapper in each `RawTransactions` entry rather than hard-coding `RawTransaction`.

reviewCommentsList.author: dangell7
reviewCommentsList.body: Done, isTxnType in DeliverMax.cpp now reads TransactionType in the three forms parseUInt16 accepts (the name, an integer, a string of digits) in 173cefbfd99efbd1ee238c13f230e3c4635ec0f5, so a numeric Batch or inner Payment gets the alias and any other value is left for STParsedJSON to reject. testDeliverMax in Batch_test.cpp signs numeric and numeric-string outer and inner types, and those four forms failed on 239126a36452db158938792c6b3b28e49151164d before the change.
